1. How are congestion control and quality of service related? ## Congestion control & QoS

- In congestion control , the load on a network is prevented from exceeding the capacity. - Quality of Service refers to the characteristics that a flow of data seeks to attain. - If there is good congestion control, then the QoS is also good and vice versa
2. What is the difference between open-loop congestion control and closed-loop congestion control?

## Open-loop vs closed-loop congestion

- Open-loop congestion control policies try to prevent congestion. - In the open loop congestion control policies are made in such a way that congestion is avoided before it occurs. This type of congestion control can be control by the source as well by the destination. The methods by which open loop is used includes the window policy, retransmission policy etc. - Closed-loop congestion control policies try to alleviate the effects of congestion
- Closed loop congestion control is used to throw out the congestion after the congestion is made or occur.

It uses method of back pressure and choke packet etc. 3. Name the policies that can prevent congestion and the policies that alleviate congestion. ## Congestion policies

- The following policies can help to prevent congestion:
- a good retransmission policy,
- use of the selective-repeat window,
- a good acknowledgment policy,
- a good discard policy, and
- a good admissions policy. - Congestion can be alleviated by
- back pressure,
- a choke point, and
- explicit signaling
4. What are the four general techniques to improve QoS??

## Techniques to improve QoS

- Scheduling,
- traffic shaping,
- admission control, and
- resource reservation
5. What is traffic shaping? Name two methods to shape traffic. ## Traffic shaping

- Traffic shaping , also known as packet shaping, is a type of network bandwidth management for the manipulation and prioritization of network traffic to reduce the impact of heavy use cases from effecting other users. - Method to shape traffic are
- the leaky bucket method and
- the token bucket method

## 6.

Explain what is DNS. ## Domain Name Servers (DNS)

- Domain Name Servers (DNS) are the Internet's equivalent of a phone book. - They maintain a directory of domain names and translate them to Internet Protocol (IP) addresses . 7. What is an advantage of a hierarchical name space over a flat name space for a system the size of the internet? ## Advantage of hierarchical name space

- When the name space is large, searching a name in hierarchical structure (tree) is much faster that searching it in a flat structure (linear).

- The first can use a binary search; the second needs to use a sequential search. ## 8. Compare between MTAs and MAAs and discuss the protocols used by each agent. ## MTAs vs MAAs

- Message Transfer Agents (MTAs) are required to send the message through the Internet. - Message Access Agents (MAAs) are required to retrieve the message at the destination computer. - The first and second stages of mail delivery (MTA client-server) use the protocol SMTP. - The third stage needs a pull protocol; the client must pull message from the server to the client.

- The third stage uses MAAs. ## 9. Explain the usage of MIME protocol. ## MIME (Multi-Purpose Internet Mail Extensions)

- MIME (Multi-Purpose Internet Mail Extensions) is an extension of the original Internet e-mail protocol that lets people use the protocol to exchange different kinds of data files on the Internet: audio, video, images, application programs, and other kinds, as well as the ASCII text handled in the original protocol, the Simple Mail Transport Protocol (SMTP)
